"You enter into my office," Ioseliani kicked him in the ribs, "Wake me the fuck up," Another kick, another terrified grunt, "And tell me I CANNOT DO SOMETHING THAT'S WRITTEN IN THE THIEF'S LAW, YOU LITTLE RUNT!" The last kick would cause Ivan to roll over on his back now holding on to both his face, blood running from his mouth and nose, the punch having made good contact. 

Jaba would lean forward, "By the Thief Laws, your actions at Vorkuta in aiding the Usoyani forces are to be considered TREACHERY, and it doesn't matter if it was BEFORE sides were chosen, so, you little fucking mongrel, don't you fucking DARE disturb my nap with your yapping when you are a clear cut traitor..." 

Ioseliani grinned, "By law, you are a nobody, got it? Not a Thief anymore... But I also did it because I fucking hate you, Ivan, and I always hated you." 

Ivan would try to scramble back only to receive a kick to the face, blood droplets hitting the floor.  

"Who gave you the right to even CONSIDER a place as a general? You were always uppity." Ioseliani spit on the floor, turning around and walking back to his armchair. 

"Alright, now get the fuck out of my sight before I blow your brains out, filthy traitor." The last part was said with a pleased demonstrative close of the eyes.

options.name: Laws are written to be abused.

title: There's Always a Bigger Dog
desc:
Artur Cohen sighed and rubbed his hands, trying to ease his nervousness. He never had the chance to return to teaching after the war had failed. No, he barely had time to save himself, to run further East, hiding his Jewish roots. 

"She just ran into my fist!" The girls in front of his desk were both students, both of them on the way to graduation. While he could not remember the name of the first one off the top of his head, the little mutt that stood to the right of her, her name he knew VERY well. Sofia Berezovskaya. 

The daughter of the local Pakhan snickered self-indulgently. "I said, SHE RAN INTO MY FIST, YOU OLD OWL!"  

Cohen considered standing up and grabbing the little bitch by the ear. 'Ran into her fist', what utter bollocks, this generation knew nothing about discipline, let alone simple empathy. 'Old owl', if he was still in the Union, she would be on cleaning duty for the next decade for insulting a teacher! 

Then his mind jumped to her father. If the principal disciplined her, what was next? Berezovskiy did not need to send an army to Cohen's door. It was simple. His papers would start 'getting lost' in the bureaucracy, the school's investors would all suddenly pull out for various reasons, local businesses would serve him badly or not serve him at all. 

"Is that true, Masha?"  

The girl with the black eye would sniffle and nod. Cohen ground his teeth but opened his mouth. 

"Then there is no more problem, return to classes." 

As the two left, Sofia would shove Masha through the door, giggling. Cohen sat back in his chair and rubbed his face. No, he would never have had the chance to rebuild a school before the Thieves came in.

title: Along the South
desc:
Ioseliani felt a sense of deja vu, as he walked into the room of generals, all of them around the map of Russia as Batov continued explaining something in a focused manner, the only light being the huge lamp in the centre of the room as it shone on every crease of the paper. 

"Planning the march East, eh?" The Great Pakhan took a swig from his bottle, walking up to the table, the generals parting to let him through, leaving only Batov standing on the opposite side of the table. 

"We certainly are." Batov responded absent-mindedly, tracing his finger on the Eastern front. 

"So, old boy, what do you have for me?" Ioseliani kicked a chair to the table, sitting down and taking on his usual bored expression. 

Batov lifted his eyes. "Well, for starters we have some good understanding of the enemy's industry centres." He traced his finger on the southern border. "The Northern climate makes it hard for any city to develop well, so going too far North, or committing more forces there will probably result in resource starvation and useless land." 

"So what do you propose?" Ioseliani had by now gotten used to Batov's self-centred style of explanation. The General knew what he was doing when it came to strategy and tended to get wrapped up in his own thoughts, the Great Pakhan just had to listen. 

Batov smiled, his eyes still on the map. "Either we use overwhelming forces to crush the clearly less-protected north and encircle the heavily armed south, or we utilize Omsk as a shield to exhaust them." 

Ioseliani grinned, getting up. "It seems you have it under control." While the phrase seemed to be directed at the whole group of generals, Batov could swear he had seen a respectful nod towards himself as the Great Pakhan departed.

options.name: Never disturb a great craftsman in his labour.

title: Greed Conquers All
desc:
Otto nervously scratched the back of his head, the aged administrator rubbing his hands as the two men in the worn SS uniforms observed the warhead that was snuck out through the service tunnels, the greyed man in a lab coat that came with them checking some parts and pieces, the Geiger counter in his hand picking up small disturbances. 

"I-is everything up to expectation?" The two men turned their heads at Otto's inquiry, one of them chuckling, while the third one continued checking the warhead. 

The nearest man in the SS uniform, the blonde, as if he came straight off of a propaganda poster, turned back to the lab-coated individual pronouncing something in Russian, Otto grimacing at the Untermensch language. 

The 'professor' lifted his head, turning off the Geiger counter and nodding. 

The blonde turned back to the administrator, sighing and unbuttoning the black jacket, Otto feeling a freezing block of ice drop into his stomach. Was he a loose end to them..? 

"P-please I have a wife, sh-she's sick, I swear it's the real thi-" The blonde came up to Otto at a leisurely pace, reaching for something in the inside jacket pocket, "P-please..." 

A stack of papers was stuffed into his hands, the administrator pausing, terror changing to surprise. 

"Shut the fuck up. Two passports to Switzerland, two 'mill' dollars on the offshore account," The blonde pronounced with a deep Russian accent, grinning. "Now fuck off, Papasha, deal is done." 

Otto wiped away the drop of cold sweat as the three turned to the nuclear-laden truck, boarding it to depart back to whatever Untermensch hellhole they were from, several joking in-between each other and laughing as they went.

options.name: Not even the Aryan man can withstand the call of Capital.

title: The Shadow State
desc:
Stepan had Volga German roots, however, in the end, the only thing that mattered was that he could speak German and had blonde hair. You wouldn't be able to get a more 'Aryan' Slav if you combed through the whole of Europe. And the Yugran bandits could not believe their luck when that 'Aryan' was found in a local bandit. 

On the other hand, Arkadiy did not look Aryan. The smuggler's black hair, brown shifty eyes, and small stature looked nothing like the posters, but in the end, Ost-Paris met the two as warmly as a breezeblock regardless. 

It was early morning, the two have already awakened in the abandoned bunker hidden within the forest floor and pulled on their smuggled SS uniforms, trying their best to not let the anxiety get to them. 

"Stepka, I'm gonna go check what's up-top, you go get the docs, got it?" Stepan nodded, turning to Arkadiy's backpack, the latter would slowly push the rusted trapdoor of the bunker open, peering through the small gap, seeing if any patrol was passing through. 

Silence... 

"I think it's-" Arkadiy would go quiet, as he heard the hurried shuffle of fallen leaves on the ground, but continued observing. 

The Frenchman must have escaped the daily march to the work camp, but the state he was in, it was surprising he could even run, his skin hanging off of him like ill-fit clothing, his eyes sunken into the skull. "Non! Non! S'il vous plait, n-" Arkadiy heard a click somewhere in the distance and- 

"There they are," Stepan finally found the documents turning back to his comrade, only to find the man sitting against the closed bunker trap door, his face ashen. 

"Arka, 'sup with you?" 

"I think..." He mumbled.

options.name: "I think we should wait for a bit..."

title: Providence Didache
desc:
"So what's the show even about?" Vlad still felt, to say the least, sceptical about Kydyr's invitation to watch a cartoon, of all things. 

In return, his bandit friend would sigh and knock some ash off of his cigarette. "Providence lore? I'm pretty sure the fuckers up in the state departments specifically made it impenetrable so that some jackboot fuck can't make sense of it." 

This did not fill Vlad with confidence as he continued to stare blindly into the screen, "Isn't there... a shortened version?" 

Kydyr paused, staring into the box of the smuggled TV, clearly trying to formulate his idea as some weirdly shaped character pummelled another weirdly shaped character. "Well... Okay, imagine every other century a lotta very rich mad fucks get together to fight to the death." 

"Right, so basically pakhans." 

"Yeah, sure, pakhans. A couple of pakhans gather up every other century and fight to the death so that the survivor can get a chance to get a wish granted to them by the Golden Fleece." 

"Aaaand, that's it..?" 

"They also summon some historical figures as their 'companions' in fights. Lotsa magical bullshit. Just roll with it..."  

Vlad was feeling unsure if he wanted to really watch it anymore... 

"So... they summon anyone?" 

"Hm? Oh yeah, Giordano Bruno, Carl Friedrich Wagner, Nevsky, Pushkin, Peter the Great..." 

"Anyone more modern?" 

"Yeah, kinda why I invited you, they're gonna reveal the Great Pakhan's companion form." 

"Companion? Wouldn't they want him to be one of the guys fighting?" 

"It's Providence lore, don't worry about it- Wait there it is!" Kydyr sat forward, "They're summoning him!" 

Vlad also sat forward, "Get outta the way you're blocking the screen!" 

"Oh shush! Lemme-" Kydyr paused, his expression turning to shock... "Gaha... GAHAHAHA!" The bandit fell back, his sides going into orbit from what he just saw. 

Vlad looked at the screen, seeing... a purple-haired... girl..? "W-why's the Great Pakhan a girl..?" He could barely contain the confused disgust in his tone. 

Kydyr sat up wiping his cheeks from the tears of laughter. "Gohoho... Oh man, Vladik, the funniest part-"

title: UNFORGIVABLE
desc:
Rafael carefully stepped into Ioseliani's office, a reflexive nervous gulp travelling down his throat. The room was a complete mess, papers lying around, some of them torn, some of them wet with what looked like whiskey stains, as if a booze-filled whirlwind burst through the room. 

"RAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAF!" The right-hand man finally noticed the Great Pakhan emptying one of the bookcases, looking for something, his usually slicked back hair in tufts, the smell of heavy booze in the air, "GET THE FUCK HERE, YOU SON OF A BITCH!" 

"H-hey, Boss..."  

Ioseliani looked up from the drawer, his eyes bloodshot, Rafael never having seen such an enraged expression on the man before. Standing up, Ioseliani would turn back to emptying the drawers, his jaw clenched. 

"Raf, who in fuck's name had let the Japanese into the propaganda department!?" 

"W-what?" 

The bookshelf would tumble to the floor with a great smash as the Great Pakhan pulled it down, looking around like a trapped beast and continuing his ruffle through the paperwork. 

"I said, WHO LET THE ASIANS INTO THE MOTHERFUCKING PROPAGANDA DEPARTMENT!?" 

Rafael blinked, trying to process. "Is there... a problem..?"  

"Yes! THAT!" Ioseliani pointed at his desk. Rafael would carefully tip-toe around the spilt papers and reach the desk. The only thing left on it was a small figurine of a... bandit? Bandit girl? The proportions were weird, eyes were slightly too big, the limbs a bit too thin, and the hair was... purple? She also seemed to look like a... teen? 

"What am I looking at, Boss?"  

"Their product! Told me they were gonna make a show, something about a good FUCKING IMAGE! GOOD IMAGE, MY BA-" Ioseliani pulled out the paper, slurring out a victorious 'Ah-ha!'. 

"OUT OF THE WAY, RAF! AND IF I SEE YOU TAKE THAT FIGURINE, YOU WILL REGRET IT FOR THE REST OF YOUR SHORT LIFE! NONE ON THIS LIST WILL LIVE TO SEE TOMORROW!" Ioseliani would burst out of the room, taking out his revolver as he went, the thing almost misfiring into his leg, leaving the right-hand man in shocked silence.

title: A Long Way From Home
desc:
Usoyan sat at his desk, his fingers interlocked, the freezing night howling powerlessly against the glass of his window, the oil lamp casting a warm glow across his office. In such moments, he would cast his mind to the past, the Old World's siren call pulling him back 

Tbilisi, 24 years old, young and inexperienced, the next thing he knew one of the pigs had grabbed him and beat him into submission. Stealing didn't give him much, and the short death row did not reform him, but it sure as Hell taught him a lot about life. 

Aslan allowed himself a thoughtful scowl as he stared into the flickering flames. The Tiflis Three were strange beasts in his eyes. On one hand, their deaths got his jailers' heads torn off, on the other hand, while he may have escaped, his homeland lay under the same monster that ruined it since he was a child.  

When the jail guards got called off to fight, it did not take long to overpower the green boys they put up instead, and then he ran... Oh he ran, he sure did. Trekking across the Caucasus, further North, past the constantly changing warlord borders, with fake names and faker currency, meeting many, remembering few. 

Usoyan shook off the nostalgia, but as his hand reached to extinguish the flame of the lamp, muttered,"Tbiliso, mzis da vardebis mkhareo..."

options.name: "Tbilisi, the side of sun and roses..."

title: Creeping Roots
desc:
"The fuck do you mean we gotta answer for every bullet!?" Valygin almost spat with rage as he slammed his rifle on the desk. 

Xatun put down the smuggled porno mag, his expression showing that he would rather be anywhere but here, explaining to some mook why the arsenal started to keep tabs. 

"Valygin, tell me, do you get paid?" 

"Well, yeah, since last month." 

"Right, so no more random looting raids. That also means that instead of letting you blockheads take any weapons and ammunition you like, we gotta collect it, mark it, sell it off..." 

"Right..." Valygin made a thinking face, Xatun continuing the logical chain. 

"So that we can buy ammo for YOUR guns, because you work for the Territory, right? And if we buy you ammo, instead of you taking it, whose ammo is it?" 

Valygin clenched his jaw.  

Xatun noticed the spark of understanding, "That's right, it's not YOUR ammo, it's OUR ammo, and if you're using OUR ammo, you're BORROWING it, you blockhead! Every time you chamber a round, that's territory budget getting fired through those skulls. And what do we do with money if we're not using it?" 

The bandit soldier sighed dejectedly, "We count it." 

"Good job, Valygin, maybe you're not completely mentally deficient! Now get out and stop bothering me,"

options.name: "Last time I heard, they'll be counting rifles soon."

title: The Unbreakables
desc:
"You look older, Diyar." Aslan noted, looking at his men unloading the trucks of equipment in the distance, the smog of the early morning factories starting up making the machines look like giant bugs. 

"And your Kurdi is rusty, brother. None of us are getting younger." Diyar took out a pack of cigarettes, putting one between his lips, Usoyan grimacing and looking away. 

"I simply wanted to offer you an exit, if you need it. I got myself land in the Russian Wastes, you can walk out of this and-" 

"And leave the sunny lands of the 'Black State' behind?" The grey-haired man lit his cigarette chuckling as he puffed on it. 

Usoyan's scowl only grew, "This cause, our cause, it's-" 

"Save your breath, brother, you'll just breathe more smog. You can tell me about how terrible Kaukasien is as much as you want, it won't matter considering I live it." Diyar would stand up, wiping his hands on the camouflage pants. 

"Georgia wasn't all great, being that to them we were not their own. But in the end, this fight, it's not just for us, brother." The old man pulled the strap of the machine gun over his shoulder, taking a few more puffs of his cigarette. 

"This isn't about being Kurdish, or Georgian, or hating the Germans. Men had stood and died to set us free again, the Tiflis Three let not one single scream when they hoisted them up. So," Diyar turned back to Usoyan. "How am I to run away when the fight is just warming up, with your guns and all?" 

"I... I do not know." Usoyan swapped his speech from Kurdi to Georgian, the older man, in turn, looking away before giving him a slap on the shoulder and grinning.  

"The fight is not over, Aslan. Not with you on our side. We will be free, brother. Just you watch us. Now go,"

options.name: "Your path in Russia awaits you, just as mine awaits me here."

title: Vultures
desc:
As the piggish mining executives argued over which parts of Russia they would rip open when the reunification is complete, Aslan realized that he truly, supremely did not care for these people. The Germans and the Japanese were more likely to use slave labor than hire Russians, and the Americans would probably underpay them. His thoughts were interrupted, however, by the first demands of the meeting; those of the large Reichswerke HG man. 

"Alright, Mr. Usoyan, we've looked over the geological data here, and..."began the man, before trailing off. His Russian was subpar. "...and we would like to mine here," he pointed out on their map as he spoke, "here, and here." He pointed to three hillside areas near the Moskowein-Russian border. With a disillusioned, if still loyal and dogmatic voice, he continued, "The Reich requests that you generously give us the mining rights for those three sites. The oil and other resources there are requested by the Reichstag itself," 

"It will be considered, my friend," Usoyan replied, as cordially as he could, for such a man, "However, I would still like to hear from the others before I make any final decision. Mr. Davenport, from Freeport McMoRan?" With his words, the American, a lean man obviously high on cocaine, stood, and pointed to a spot on the Kamchatka peninsula. 

"It says here that diamond and borax deposits center at this point, where my finger is? We wanna mine right there, yeah. You'll let us?" 

"Again, my friend, we must hear the requests of all parties," Usoyan replied, with more control than with the German, "Mr. Aso, you actually run the mining company you represent, what do you wish to mine?" Takakishi Aso, head of the Aso mining company, rather than pointing on the map, began his request; 

"There's a hill near the Manchurian border, one with a yellowish scar on its side. We wish to run our mine on that hill, which is located..." He pointed to a hill on the map, some 290 kilometers away from the border, "...right there." 

Usoyan stood for a moment, giving the appearance of deep thought. However, the mining operations were far from his thoughts; of course these people could mine there, even the Germans! They had no clue how much money they were going to make him. He finally answered; 

"Gentlemen, you have the permission of our organization to mine where you have each requested. The Reich, the Sphere, and the free world will have their mines." With those words, Usoyan walked out, and several underlings rushed to each of the executives, giving them dozens of forms and paperwork to sign. 

For the first time in a while, Usoyan smiled.

title: Just Business
desc:
"Prost!" Abs lifted the champagne glass, gnawing on his usual cigar, his little eyes darting from one company man to another, a knowing grin trudging up to his lips. 

"Prest!" Flick slurred, the corporation leader certainly had too many whiskies, his usual fiery temper now flickering in all directions like a flame in a strong wind, the glass between his fingers in a very unsure position. 

"Prost." Geilenberg looked the most modest of them all, the glass of German beer being quite symbolic for the state-corporation puppet. 

"Certainly!" Siemens even stood up a little, his glass of wine held with a steady hand, but his cheeks slightly red, the old man also having relaxed with the coming of alcohol. 

"And to the destruction of those fu-!" Flick opened his mouth, about to go on another rant. 

"Yes yes, Friedrich, 'the lesser races', but let the guest of honour speak first." Abs interrupted, stopping the situation from devolving further, curiously waiting for the last corporation leader to raise a toast. 

Usoyan grimaced as he looked at his new business partners, and picked up his glass of water, uninterested in alcohol. 

"Well, gentlemen, I suppose, prost." 

Abs was almost glimmering, "To future success!"

title: Time for a rebrand
desc:
Air was filled with cigar smoke. Radio played old, slow music while Usoyan sat in his office, looking outside the window. He spectated the scene outside, soldiers marching towards their duties, while on street people walked around, going to their jobs or going home. He had a big proud smile on his face. He ruled them all, high above the others in a way he only dreamed of as a boy.

 His calm was broken as someone knocked at the door. "Come in!" Usoyan shouted as he turned around to face the doors. It was Devdari, his right hand man.  "Everything is ready Sir. We are waiting for you to arrive."

"Ah Devdari, my good old Devdari..." He said while lighting up another cigar."You see all this? Do you see what we hold in our hand? This power that...some leaders would be able just to dream about?" He got up from a chair."After all these years of fighting... it is time for a big move, for a big centralization. It is time to rebrand our company." As he finished his little speech, he proceeded to the meeting that Devdari informed him about.

options.name: A toast to our future investments

title: Our biggest venture
desc:
Usoyan, dressed in all formals with a proud smile, headed towards the conference room. As he entered the room, all politicians and generals sitting at the table stood up, greeting him with respect. He sat at the head of the table. Silence spread through the room, with only the sound of papers moving being heard.

"Gentlemen!" he said, clearing his throat,"I think it's finally a time for us to speak about our opponents in Siberia. Our mighty state grew stronger over the recent period of time, and we can - we should - start preparing for the war that I see as the biggest one yet! But, we must not underestimate our opponents, who used these years to build up their own military and industry, thus posing a big threat to us. But let us not be discouraged by that sight - we will crush not only our most immediate adversaries, but every other madman that would dare to stand in our way towards the final and utmost conquest of all Russian lands!"

A small comotion appeared as he made a pause in his speech. Some people didn't accept it well, while others looked at him with a more or less well-hidden smile. Whispers filled the room, slightly breaking the silence. Then Usoyan continued talking.

"Gentlemen, I hereby advise that we immediately start preparing ourselves for the upcoming storm. We need our factories pumping out more guns, our men tough as steel, our generals ready to lead these same men into the battle! This said, the meeting is over. The fate of this country rests upon your shoulders, so don't screw this up." After a brief moment of silence, Usoyan stood up and left the room with a quick step. The rest of the men present remained there for another couple of minutes, discussing what they just heard.

options.name: "This is going to be tough, my friend!"
